real_defects.issue: Waiver detection tested the whole sentence, so 'A 5% bid bond and proof of insurance are required, but a site visit is not required.' reported the bond and insurance as 'appears to say it is not required' (the same for 'X is required while Y is not required'). A bidder trusting it could skip a bond and be rejected. Fixed: negation is read in the clause holding the keyword (split at but/however/whereas/while/although/though/except that), and a stated requirement in that clause outweighs a waiver.

'Firms with no local office will be required to attend the mandatory site visit.' matched the 'no ... will be required' waiver, so a mandatory site visit read as waived. Fixed: that branch no longer matches when 'to' follows ('required to attend' is an obligation).
'No pre-bid site visit will be held.' was not read as a waiver because the word pattern \w+ stopped at the hyphen. Fixed with [\w-]+ (conservative direction: it showed 'found', not 'waived').
